draft.title: Transformations and symmetry
card: Translation
slides a shape without turning or flipping it. Every point moves the same distance in the same direction.
Reflection
flips a shape over a mirror line. The image is the same size but faces the other way.
Rotation
turns a shape about a point by an angle, such as 90° or 180°. Dilation resizes a shape by a scale factor.

A shape has line symmetry if a mirror line splits it into two matching halves. It has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a turn of less than 360°. A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 6.
draft.remember: Slide, flip, turn or resize. Symmetry means the shape matches itself after a flip or a turn.

a.q: Maya moves a tile pattern by sliding every tile 3 cm right, with no turning or flipping. Which transformation is this?
a.why: Sliding every point the same distance in the same direction is a translation. A reflection is wrong because nothing is flipped over a mirror line.
a.clue: Nothing is flipped, turned or resized.

b.q: A logo is an equilateral triangle. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
b.why: A line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side splits the triangle into matching halves, so there are 3 lines. The answer 6 is tempting, but that is the order of rotational symmetry of a hexagon, not of this triangle.
b.clue: Draw a line from each corner to the opposite side.

problems.detail: The stem says 'sliding' with 'no turning or flipping', which repeats the card's definition of translation almost word for word. The clue then rules out the other three options too, so a student can answer by matching words without understanding the idea.
The clue 'Draw a line from each corner to the opposite side' all but gives the answer away: a triangle has 3 corners, so a student can count 3 lines without understanding line symmetry.

proposal.title: Transformations and symmetry
card: Translation
slides a shape without turning or flipping it. Every point moves the same distance in the same direction.
Reflection
flips a shape over a mirror line. The image is the same size but faces the other way.
Rotation
turns a shape about a fixed point by an angle. A quarter turn is 90° and a half turn is 180°. Dilation, the fourth type, resizes a shape by a scale factor.

A shape has line symmetry if folding it along a line makes the two halves match exactly. It has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a turn of less than 360°. A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 6.
proposal.remember: Slide, flip, turn or resize. Symmetry means the shape matches itself after a flip or a turn.

a.q: The hour hand of a clock moves from pointing at 12 to pointing at 3. Which transformation describes this move?
opts: A 90° rotation about the centre of the clock
A 180° rotation about the centre of the clock
A reflection in the line from 12 to 6
A translation of the hand to the right
a.why: The hand stays fixed at the centre and turns a quarter of the way round, from 12 to 3, which is 90°. A 180° rotation would take it to 6. A translation is wrong because it would move the whole hand, including the end at the centre.
a.clue: Does the hand stay joined at the centre of the clock?

b.q: A door panel is a rectangle that is longer than it is wide. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
b.why: Folding across the middle, either lengthwise or widthwise, gives matching halves, so there are 2 lines. The answer 4 is tempting, but folding along a diagonal of a non-square rectangle does not make the halves match exactly.
b.clue: Picture each possible fold and check the halves match exactly.

a.best: A 90° rotation about the centre of the clock
